title: Early New Orleans clarinet players
summary: Duhé lists early clarinetists, including Zeno, Manuel Perez and Big Eye Louis Nelson, who led on C clarinet.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Can you tell us about the old style clarinet players? The first ones you heard, different style. Who were some of the better players that you heard?
Well, we had Willie Warner. Yeah. And Frank Gwynn. That old one. Zed. Zed. Kaiser. Kaiser. Kaiser.
I heard Fess talk about Zed a lot. Yeah. And Manuel Mineta.
Did you ever play with Manuel Mineta? Oh, yeah. We played in Storerville, one or two years.
I told him yesterday we were coming up to see you and he said to say hello to you.
Yeah, Manuel and Peter Bucow and all that bunch from across the river there.
I wondered about the early clarinetists. Did they sometimes play more of the lead or did they always play that part of the chorus?
I'm going to tell you, at that time, big ol' Louis was the clarinet man in New Orleans. Yeah, it was tops. He played the lead because he used the C clarinet, played the violin part.

And Teal. George Mackey. George Mackey. But George Mackey. Lawrence and Teal. Yeah, they played B and A clarinet, but Louis used only C, played the violin, played the violin part. Yeah. He played the lead sheet all the time.
